additional_info.subject: ID0439171-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / RN 170002791] Incorrect settlement of charging session CRM:02919000217
additional_info.body:
Hi Szymon,
I checked the logs and there is no logs after our 09:07
From our point of view, we can only refer to a problem upstream, because even if the mainbreaker opened during charging, the PLC is able to send the logs afterwards.
But here we are not seeing any kind of logs. Do you know if there was any problem upstream on the cabinet or related?
From our side, I can only check if EcoG should be able to record the values even in such a critical situation as grid failure.
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0439171-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / RN 170002791] Incorrect settlement of charging session CRM:02919000217

As far as I know, there was no problem with the power supply there. The second station at this location behaved in the same way at the same time:
ID:  RKvLvM

Best regards,
Szymon

additional_info.subject: ID0439171-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / RN 170002791] Incorrect settlement of charging session CRM:02919000217
additional_info.body:
Hello Szymon,
From the first charger, when the logs come in, there is a huge time gap between them that is not filled:
And when searching for the Transaction ID, the ecoG reports a power loss error:
2025-07-16T11:29:11.597922+00:00 [FW070006G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/7844d90536e2[739]: OCPP: Send command: StopTransaction (06657a82-264b-470f-bef5-b604cdcc92d3) - {"meterStop":2510307,"timestamp":"2025-07-16T11:29:11.592Z","transactionData":[],"reason":"PowerLoss","transactionId":1215926388}
From this 2nd charger you gave to me, there was no charging session ongoing during the shutdown, you can search from 8:00 UTC to 9:10 UTC, there are only heartbeat logs. It crashes at the almost the same time 09:06:45.
When it recovers, it also has the same behaviour as the charger on top, there is a huge gap in the logs timestamps which is not filled.
Unfortunately, I cannot prove where the root cause is since there are no logs, from my perspective, it's very unlikely that 2 PLCs at the exact same time crashed in totally different conditions of usage (one charging, one standby).
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco
